ORLY.one_line: Auto-parts retailer for DIY and pro mechanics; moat from store density, inventory depth and non-discretionary repair demand.
ORLY.reason: Defensive, high-return compounder with mid-teens forward EPS growth; 24.3x NTM P/E is fair given consistency, and 25% street upside follows a sharp pullback.

EBAY.one_line: Online marketplace pivoting to focused categories (collectibles, motors, refurbished) and first-party ads to reaccelerate GMV.
EBAY.reason: Q2'26 GMV +14% (US GMV +24%), ad revenue +25%, EPS growth 41% - the turnaround is working and 16.5x NTM P/E no longer looks 'demanding' as the prior model tag suggested.

red_flags: Macau VIP hold miss temporarily depressed Q2 EBITDA (one-off, not structural)
LVS.one_line: Owns the Macau mass-market recovery plus the Singapore monopoly asset, Marina Bay Sands.
LVS.reason: Marina Bay Sands EBITDA of $689M and Sands China mass GGR +8% (beating the Macau market's +4%) show core strength; 11.5x NTM P/E with 51.5% street upside is a rare quality-plus-cheapness combination.

red_flags: Elevated leverage, 5.7x net debt/EBITDA - monitor covenant headroom against new-project capex (incl. UAE)
WYNN.one_line: Pure-play Macau/Las Vegas casino operator riding the Macau mass-market recovery.
WYNN.reason: Wynn Palace mass GGR +25.9% YoY and Macau operating revenue +13.7% show an accelerating recovery; 17x NTM P/E with 62.7% street upside is deep value if leverage stays manageable.

GRMN.one_line: Diversified GPS/wearables hardware maker across fitness, aviation, marine and auto-OEM segments.
GRMN.reason: Excellent multi-segment franchise (Fitness +42%, 24.5% margins) but the stock already reflects it - only 2.7% street upside at 27.1x NTM P/E leaves little margin of safety.

red_flags: $150M charge tied to First Brands Group bankruptcy distorts trailing P/E (518x) and ROE - credit/counterparty exposure in the industrial distribution book
GPC.one_line: NAPA auto-parts and industrial distributor; headline multiples distorted by a one-time bankruptcy-related charge.
GPC.reason: Underlying 2026 adjusted EPS guidance implies only ~5% growth once the one-off is excluded; 15.9x NTM P/E is fair but not compelling for mid-single-digit growth.

HD.one_line: Dominant home-improvement retailer expanding into professional contractor supply via SRS Distribution.
HD.reason: Pro segment is offsetting soft DIY demand (comps +1.7%, Pro outperforming); 18.7x NTM P/E with 28.6% target upside offers a best-in-class way to play an eventual housing-turnover recovery.

red_flags: FY26 guidance cut (flat comps, sales trimmed to ~$92B) on continued DIY weakness
LOW.one_line: #2 home-improvement retailer pushing deeper into Pro and online after cutting FY26 guidance.
LOW.reason: Despite the cut, Pro/online delivered a fifth straight positive-comp quarter; 14.8x NTM P/E with 32.7% target upside prices in most of the bad news already.

red_flags: Sector-wide affordability/tariff headwinds - flat revenue, rising incentives/buydowns
DHI.one_line: Largest US homebuilder; asset-light land-option model seen as best-positioned through the affordability downturn.
DHI.reason: Low leverage (1.2x) and 12.6% ROE reflect the highest-quality homebuilder economics in the group; 12.4x NTM P/E for a cyclical trough merits full diligence as the top way to play eventual rate relief.

red_flags: Revenue -8.7% YoY, negative street target-price upside (-2.5%) - analysts see further downside, not value
LEN.one_line: Second-largest homebuilder; more land-heavy strategy, underperforming peers in the current downturn.
LEN.reason: Unlike DHI/PHM/NVR, Lennar's margins and revenue are deteriorating faster than peers and the Street sees downside at current price - the weakest homebuilder in this batch.

red_flags: Revenue -10.9% YoY amid sector-wide housing downturn
NVR.one_line: Ultra capital-light homebuilder (land options, no owned land bank) with the industry's best returns on capital.
NVR.reason: Zero-debt, 31.5% ROE model is the highest-quality balance sheet among homebuilders; 16.2x NTM P/E is reasonable for that quality even in a cyclical trough.

PHM.one_line: Move-up and active-adult focused homebuilder, less exposed to the entry-level affordability crunch than peers.
PHM.reason: Low leverage (0.4x) and a diversified buyer mix cushion the downturn; 11.1x NTM P/E with 17.5% target upside is attractive for a well-run builder.

WSM.one_line: Premium home-furnishings retailer (Pottery Barn, West Elm, Williams Sonoma) with raised FY26 comp guidance.
WSM.reason: Excellent execution (all brands positive comps, guidance raised) but the stock is already up 18% on it, leaving only 6.9% street upside at 22.6x NTM P/E - confirms the prior 'excessive' tag.

red_flags: Fuel-cost pressure noted by analysts; net debt/EBITDA still 3.3x
CCL.one_line: Largest cruise operator, deleveraging while riding still-strong Caribbean/Bahamas demand.
CCL.reason: 16.5% forward EPS growth and improving margins at just 8.8x NTM P/E, with 52.8% street upside, look attractive despite negative 1-year momentum tied to fuel-cost worries.

EXPE.one_line: Online travel platform with an accelerating, high-margin B2B white-label business now in its 20th straight quarter of double-digit growth.
EXPE.reason: B2B Gross Bookings +21%, EBITDA margin expanding, guidance raised again; 11.2x NTM P/E for 53.8% forward EPS growth is one of the most mispriced names in the batch.

HLT.one_line: Global hotel franchisor with a record 527,000-room pipeline and a raised RevPAR outlook.
HLT.reason: Strong fundamentals (6-7% net unit growth, RevPAR raised to 2-3%) are already in the price - only 12.4% street upside at 31.1x NTM P/E and 4.2x leverage leave little cushion.

MAR.one_line: World's largest hotel company by rooms, benefiting from luxury demand and the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
MAR.reason: Fundamentals are excellent (RevPAR outlook raised twice this year) but the stock is up 32.3% over the past year with only 8.2% further upside at 27.6x NTM P/E - priced for the good news.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 6.1x, the highest of the cruise peer group; FCF yield -25%; guided to flat/declining net yields amid self-inflicted 40% YoY Caribbean capacity growth
NCLH.one_line: Third-largest cruise line, adding Caribbean capacity faster than pricing can absorb it.
NCLH.reason: Weakest balance sheet and pricing power in the cruise group - management already guided yields down; leverage stress is disqualifying despite the cheap 8.9x P/E.

RCL.one_line: Best-in-class cruise operator (Icon/Star of the Seas), now leading Carnival in forward bookings for the first time.
RCL.reason: Roughly two-thirds of 2026 capacity already booked at record rates and industry-leading 23.5% margins, yet trades at just 12.4x NTM P/E with 43.5% street upside - the strongest cruise pick in the batch.

red_flags: FY26 comp guidance cut mid-year from +1% to +3% to -1% to flat; tariff margin pressure and weak pet category
TSCO.one_line: Rural lifestyle retailer (farm/ranch supply) that cut FY26 guidance mid-year on tariffs and pet-category softness.
TSCO.reason: Growth has stalled and management just lowered guidance for the second time this year - the modest 16.2x NTM multiple isn't enough compensation given the deteriorating trend.

red_flags: Comp growth decelerated from double digits to 3.8%; Sephora expanding aggressively inside Kohl's
ULTA.one_line: Leading beauty specialty retailer facing intensifying Sephora/Kohl's competition after years of double-digit growth.
ULTA.reason: Still growing (comps +3.8%, guided 2.5-6.5% for FY26) with a strong 46.1% ROE at a reasonable 17.6x NTM P/E and 15.7% upside - worth full diligence on whether share losses to Sephora stabilize.

red_flags: Three consecutive quarters of negative comps, driven by traffic/frequency declines
CMG.one_line: Fast-casual burrito chain with best-in-class unit economics, now in its third straight quarter of negative comps.
CMG.reason: 49.6% ROE and management's refusal to discount suggest a demand air-pocket rather than a structural break; 23.9x NTM P/E with 40% target upside merits full diligence on whether traffic stabilizes.

red_flags: Leverage 4.8x is structurally high by design of the securitization funding model, not distress-driven
DPZ.one_line: Global pizza franchisor (asset-light, securitized-debt model) growing orders while the stock has lagged.
DPZ.reason: Orders and international unit growth remain positive even as the stock fell 17.4% over the year; 14.3x NTM P/E for high-teens EPS growth and 29% target upside looks like value in a franchise-quality name.

red_flags: US comp growth decelerated to 0.8% on traffic softness
MCD.one_line: The largest global QSR franchisor, leaning on value-menu promotions (McValue) to defend traffic.
MCD.reason: Even with decelerating US traffic, the franchise moat, 31.7% margins and international growth support double-digit EPS growth; 17.4x NTM P/E with 26.8% upside is attractive for the highest-quality name in the group.

SBUX.one_line: Coffee chain executing a real operational turnaround under CEO Brian Niccol - comps accelerating for four straight quarters.
SBUX.reason: Q3 comps +7.9% (vs. Street's 5.7% estimate) and FY26 EPS guidance raised twice; at 30.4x NTM P/E the turnaround is partly priced in, but 18.3% remaining target upside still justifies full diligence.

red_flags: Data card shows forward EPS growth of -12% vs. trailing, inconsistent with reported margin/revenue strength - needs reconciliation against company guidance in full diligence, likely a comp-base or one-time-item effect
YUM.one_line: KFC/Taco Bell/Pizza Hut franchisor with the strongest revenue growth (+12.2%) and margins (25.4%) in the restaurant group.
YUM.reason: Best-in-class international unit growth and margins support the case, but the negative headline forward-EPS figure must be checked against guidance before sizing; 20.4x NTM P/E with 24.7% upside is still reasonable.

DASH.one_line: Dominant US food-delivery platform expanding into grocery/retail and international (Deliveroo) with improving margins.
DASH.reason: 35.6% revenue growth and rising EBITDA margins (2.8% of GOV, up from 2.7%) justify a growth premium; 48.6x NTM P/E is rich in absolute terms but reasonable relative to the growth trajectory.

red_flags: SEC accounting/disclosure fraud settlement (Jan 2026, $40M penalty plus individual executive sanctions) for inflating Nutrition segment profit; DOJ closed its criminal probe with no charges
ADM.one_line: Global grain/oilseed processor recovering from a 2024 accounting scandal, settled with the SEC in January 2026.
ADM.reason: 14.4x NTM P/E for a crush-margin rebound looks cheap, but thin 2.2% margins, commodity-cycle earnings and a recent governance scandal keep quality and growth conviction too low to advance despite the valuation.

red_flags: Net debt/EBITDA 5.2x and FCF yield -30.9% - debt not well covered by operating cash flow during Viterra integration per analyst commentary
BG.one_line: Post-merger Bunge/Viterra global agribusiness giant carrying high leverage and deeply negative free cash flow during integration.
BG.reason: Headline 88%/143% revenue/EPS growth is merger-driven, not organic, and leverage plus cash burn during integration is a real risk; not enough quality conviction to advance despite the low headline P/E.

COST.one_line: Best-in-class membership warehouse retailer with roughly 93% renewal rates and unmatched scale buying power.
COST.reason: Excellent business, but 40.2x NTM P/E and a 1.5% FCF yield price in near-perfection, leaving only 15.1% street upside - valuation, not the business, is the obstacle to advancing.

WMT.one_line: World's largest retailer, now compounding via e-commerce, advertising and Walmart+ membership on top of core grocery.
WMT.reason: Same story as Costco - genuinely strong growth engines (ads, e-commerce) but 34.7x NTM P/E and a 0.8% FCF yield leave little margin of safety at today's price.
